subject: EU latency variance, SLA clarification & renewal expansion
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara@cloudscale.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@cloudscale.com>
Date: 2027-05-01 09:12 -0700
Subject: Sudden EU latency variance — need SLA clarification ahead of renewal

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Quick context: over the last 36 hours we've seen repeated tail-latency spikes in the eu-west-1 region that impacted inference times for our EU customers. We're attaching a CSV with request-level timings (cloudscale_uptime_Q1.csv) — note the 95th/99th percentile divergences on May 1st.

This is timely because our annual renewal for Redwood services is scheduled for May 20. Team is open to an expansion (additional seats + higher throughput), but procurement is pressing us for clarity on:
- root cause for the regional variance
- whether this constitutes an SLA breach and the credit policy
- what mitigations RedWood can commit to (regional capacity, dedicated pool, or routing guarantees) if we upgrade to a premium tier

Can we get a quick written position and a proposed commercial path (credit + pilot for premium/dedicated) by EOD Monday? If so we'll share the packet with Procurement and Legal.

Attachments: cloudscale_uptime_Q1.csv (CSV, 84KB)

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lopez
Head of Platform Reliability | CloudScale Inc
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@cloudscale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden EU latency variance — need SLA clarification ahead of renewal

Sara — thanks for the data. I pulled the initial logs and we've started a short investigation with infra + serving runtime to correlate kernel dispatch and autoscaler activity in eu-west-1. Preliminary note: we saw small KV-cache thrashing patterns during the spikes, which can amplify tail latency on cold prefixes. I'm attaching a short preliminary review (prelim_uptime_review.pdf).

Commercially — we don't want this to stall your renewal. Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We'll propose a one-time invoice credit while we finish the RCA (I'm proposing a provisional 10% credit pending confirmation).
2) Offer an 8-week premium pilot (dedicated pool in eu-west-1) with agreed-on SLOs for regional p95/p99 latency.
3) Create an SLA amendment that formalizes the pilot SLOs, credits, and rollback/fallback behaviors.

If that sounds reasonable let's schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to confirm timelines. Marissa & Steph — any objections to the provisional credit + pilot approach?

Attachments: prelim_uptime_review.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01 13:18 -07:00
Subject: Internal: recommended commercial response for CloudScale (EU spikes)

Internal thoughts / for the record:
- Accept the technical framing (KV-cache thrash + autoscaler edge case). Ops should own mitigations and a timeline (2 weeks to implement a hotfix + autoscaler tuning).
- Commercial ask: procurement will want dollar-level numbers. For momentum on renewal + expansion we should provide: one-time credit (10-15% range), an 8-week dedicated EU pilot priced at a discounted committed rate, and a documented SLA amendment that includes rollback triggers.
- I'll own the commercial proposal and negotiate the final credit. Karthik, can you prepare a pricing sketch for a 12-week commitment at 50% capacity of their current usage (we can call it a pilot discount)?

No objections to Priyom's call plan — recommend we keep the provisional credit language soft until Ops confirms RCA.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lopez <sara@cloudscale.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@cloudscale.com>, CloudScale Legal <legal@cloudscale.com>
Date: 2027-05-02 09:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden EU latency variance — need SLA clarification ahead of renewal

Thanks — that approach is helpful and appreciated. Procurement briefed me: they will accept a provisional credit combined with a pilot, provided the SLA amendment includes clear p95/p99 commitments and an escalation path (including a dedicated pool guarantee or failover routing to another region).

Next items from our side:
- Please send a draft SLA amendment and SOW for the pilot so our legal/procurement can review.
- We're attaching a draft SOW that outlines our pilot acceptance criteria (CloudScale_SOW_draft.docx).
- Procurement requested that any credit be applied to the first invoice post-renewal and be visible on the invoice line item.

Can the pilot start by May 10 (to allow us to validate before the billing cycle)? Procurement is pushing for timeline certainty.

Attachments: CloudScale_SOW_draft.docx (DOCX, 46KB)

—Sara
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@cloudscale.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04 17:32 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden EU latency variance — need SLA clarification ahead of renewal

Sara — quick update and formal response after internal approvals:

1) Credit: Redwood will provide a one-time invoice credit equal to 12% of your next monthly invoice (applied as a line-item credit post-renewal). This is a one-time commercial concession tied to the event window described in your CSV.

2) Pilot & timeline: We can run an 8-week dedicated EU pilot starting May 10. Pilot includes a dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1, enhanced tracing hooks, and weekly status syncs. If operationally we confirm the fixes (KV-cache hotfix + autoscaler tuning) within two weeks we'll push the change to your pilot environment.

3) SLA amendment: Attached SLA amendment (sla_amendment_v1.pdf) formalizes the pilot SLOs (regional p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms), credit formula for future breaches, and an escalation path to our on-call engineering. This is a draft — legal teams can iterate.

4) Commercial pilot pricing: Karthik — pricing sketch in the HubSpot deal (linked). Karthik, please produce a contract-ready SOW and pricing table for the 8-week pilot and a follow-on 12-week committed option at the discounted rate.

5) Next: Once CloudScale confirms acceptance, we'll route the SLA amendment and SOW via DocuSign and push the pilot ticket to infra with the May 10 start date.

Links/attachments: sla_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF, 90KB); HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890; DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/abc123

Thanks — looking forward to getting you back to predictable latency and moving the renewal forward.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Success Manager | Redwood Inference
